why: Deliberate, and here the frozen side is not even a Remote Compose taxonomy: `remoteM3Catalog` never declares a componentMenu of its own, so it inherits the packaged Material 3 one wholesale — Scaffolds, Layout, Navigation, Text inputs — shelf names for a catalog of widget containers, shaders and typefaces. The policy states :remote-catalog's own @CatalogComponent(group = ...) vocabulary, led by Widget Container and Scaffold templates because a Remote design starts from a container and everything else goes inside one. RE-REVIEWED after yschimke/wear-m3-catalog#410: `Selection buttons`, `Edge-hugging buttons`, `Sliders` and `Steppers` are declared only in `src/snapshot/kotlin`, so the released-lane order never named them and under the snapshot lane the editor appended all four after every ordered group and sorted them alphabetically. Added in place — the three button families together after `Buttons`, then the two value pickers — so the stated order is the one a person sees.

The catalog states a `wasm` surface the frozen catalog omits entirely, and native agrees on fidelity/backend with only the `reason` rewritten. The addition is the point rather than a discrepancy to tolerate: the builder's Wasm canvas has no Remote Compose player, so a design drawn there is a widget-host frame with placeholders inside it and NOT a picture of what the player will produce. The frozen catalog says nothing about that, which leaves a person reading an approximate canvas with no statement that it is approximate — precisely the silence this contract moves into the repository that can answer it. Both values are pinned, so a later change to either side re-surfaces this for review.

wasm.reason: A Remote Compose document is played, not composed. The builder's Wasm canvas has no player, so it draws the widget host frame and placeholders inside it; what the player would draw is a different picture, produced by a different program from the same document.

native.reason: The generated creation-DSL Kotlin compiled against this module's own alpha Remote Compose trio and rasterised by the real player — the same lane that produces every sticker in this catalog.

why: As with wear-m3, the frozen catalog carries no label. 'RemoteCompose' is the name the catalog and its documents use; the platform word `remote-compose` would title-case to 'Remote-compose', which is not what anybody calls it.

The frozen catalog names no adapter, and this is the one place the two Wear catalogs genuinely differ: a Remote Compose widget is drawn into a host container of fixed size, not onto a watch face, so `frame/widget-host` rather than the sibling's `frame/round-screen`. Reviewed against the renderer's own remote branch, which draws exactly that.

The two host sizes, which the server carries as constants (216x76 and 216x124) and the frozen catalog does not state. Unlike the Wear padding these are DECLARED rather than measured: remote-catalog/src/main/kotlin/.../WidgetContainerPreviews.kt pins @Preview(widthDp = 216, heightDp = 76) and (216, 124), and every widget sticker renders at one of them. Reviewed against those annotations — the preview contract is the source, so a drift would break the stickers before it reached a design.

Stated as null, deliberately. remote-catalog's own policy says why: a Remote widget is written in the creation DSL rather than in Compose, which is a `code.language` and a set of structural templates, and both arrive with the template engine rather than ahead of it. Until then the export prints call sites from the record. The frozen catalog states no code block either, so this records that the absence was read rather than overlooked.
Empty for the same reason `code` is null — there is no template engine yet, so there are no structural templates to name. Recorded so a future non-empty value re-surfaces here for review.

DELIBERATE, as of this change, and it was a stated cutover blocker before it: the loss is accepted so the published catalog can serve traffic rather than waiting on a component the catalog does not draw. The frozen shelf carries `remote-m3/lottie` on Content and the published catalog cannot offer it — it is an asset player rather than a Remote Compose component call, so no record entry exists, and `remote-m3/` is not one of the donor namespaces (`layout/`, `shape/`, `asset/`, `remote-compose/`) that ProductionUiBuilderRuntime unions back in. It is one of five the swap loses and the only one of those five that RemoteContentEmitter can actually write, which is why it was the blocker rather than one more absence.

What accepting it costs, stated so nobody rediscovers it as a surprise: a new author cannot place a Lottie animation in a Remote design, and an existing document containing one fails validation as UNKNOWN_COMPONENT. Restoring it is work in wear-m3-catalog rather than here — the catalog has to draw a Lottie sticker and declare the shelf for it, per PublishedRemoteM3CatalogEquivalenceTest.knownAbsent. Tracked in https://github.com/yschimke/compose-preview-server/issues/795.
